Summarise value-of-information results

summary.voipred_voi.Rd

print() shows the results at the first thresholds; summary() gives the main findings:

  • EVPI (evpi(), e): where EVPI is positive and where it is largest, and EVPI and relative EVPI at each threshold;

  • P(useful) (e$p_useful, from evpi()): the thresholds where P(useful) is above 0.95, between 0.5 and 0.95, and below 0.5, and with thresholds, P(useful) at each of them;

  • P(best) (e$p_best, from evpi()): the most likely best strategy along the thresholds, and P(best) of each strategy;

  • EVSI (evsi()): the share of EVPI that a future study of each size recovers (EVSI / EVPI), at the thresholds with the largest EVPI.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evpi'
print(x, n = 10, per = getOption("voipred.per", 1), ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evpi'
summary(object, thresholds = NULL, per = getOption("voipred.per", 1), ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evsi'
print(x, n = 10, per = getOption("voipred.per", 1), ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evsi'
summary(object, thresholds = NULL, per = getOption("voipred.per", 1), ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_p_useful'
print(x, n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_p_useful'
summary(object, thresholds = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_p_best'
print(x, n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_p_best'
summary(object, thresholds = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evpi'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  per = getOption("voipred.per", 1),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evsi'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  per = getOption("voipred.per", 1),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_p_useful'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'voipred_p_best'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

n

Number of thresholds printed. Default 10.

per

Scale of EVPI and EVSI: the number of patients they are expressed per. Default 1 (per patient); e.g. per = 100000 gives the expected gain in net true positives per 100,000 patients. print() and summary() show EVPI (and EVSI) on that scale, and the header says so; as.data.frame() keeps the per-patient columns and adds the scaled ones, named <column>_per_<per> (e.g. EVPI_per_100000). Relative EVPI and the probabilities (P(useful), P(best), EVSI / EVPI) have no unit and are never scaled. The result itself is always per patient. The default can be set once with options(voipred.per = 100000).

...

Not used.

object, x

A result of evpi() or evsi(), or the P(useful) or P(best) of a result e of evpi() (e$p_useful, e$p_best).

thresholds

Optional thresholds to show (among those of the result). Default: all (the first 10 are printed); for evsi(), the 3 with the largest EVPI; for P(useful), none (only the bands), and with thresholds also P(useful) at each of them.

row.names, optional

Not used (as in as.data.frame()).

Value

summary(): an object of class summary.<class>, printed as shown. as.data.frame(): the estimates data frame.

Details

as.data.frame() returns the full results (the estimates).

The tables have the same layout everywhere: one row per threshold and model (P(useful)), strategy (P(best)) or future sample size (evsi()), in a column of that name, with the values in columns of fixed names (p_useful, p_best, EVSI and EVPI); evpi() has one row per threshold. print() and summary() sort the rows by threshold, and print the first n thresholds.

See also

evpi(), evsi()

Examples

df_dev_binary <- gusto[1:5000, ]
df_val_binary <- gusto[5001:5500, ]
fit1 <- glm(day30 ~ age + Killip + sysbp + pulse,
            family = binomial, data = df_dev_binary)
df_val_binary$p1 <- predict(fit1, newdata = df_val_binary, type = "response")
fit2 <- glm(day30 ~ age, family = binomial, data = df_dev_binary)
df_val_binary$p2 <- predict(fit2, newdata = df_val_binary, type = "response")
z <- seq(0.01, 0.3, by = 0.01)
res1 <- nb_val(data = df_val_binary,
               predicted_risk = df_val_binary$p1,
               outcome = "day30",
               thresholds = z,
               label = "Full")
res2 <- nb_val(data = df_val_binary,
               predicted_risk = df_val_binary$p2,
               outcome = "day30",
               thresholds = z,
               label = "Age only")
set.seed(1)
e <- evpi(res1, res2)
e
#> EVPI: Full, Age only; binary, n = 500, prior improper Beta(0, 0), 1000 posterior draws
#> 
#>  threshold      EVPI rEVPI
#>       0.01 0.0009783   Inf
#>       0.02 0.0005761 1.297
#>       0.03 0.0003607 1.491
#>       0.04 0.0000016   Inf
#>       0.05 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.06 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.07 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.08 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.09 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.10 0.0000000   Inf
#> # 20 more rows; use summary() or as.data.frame()
#> # From the same draws: P(useful) in $p_useful, P(best) in $p_best
summary(e)
#> EVPI: Full, Age only; binary, n = 500, prior improper Beta(0, 0), 1000 posterior draws
#> EVPI > 0 at 0.01-0.04; largest 0.0009783 at 0.01
#> 
#>  threshold      EVPI rEVPI
#>       0.01 0.0009783   Inf
#>       0.02 0.0005761 1.297
#>       0.03 0.0003607 1.491
#>       0.04 0.0000016   Inf
#>       0.05 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.06 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.07 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.08 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.09 0.0000000   Inf
#>       0.10 0.0000000   Inf
#> # 20 more rows; summary(x, thresholds = ) to choose
summary(e$p_useful)
#> P(useful): Full, Age only; binary, n = 500, prior improper Beta(0, 0), 1000 posterior draws
#> Thresholds where the probability that the model is useful is:
#> 
#>     model P > 0.95 0.5 to 0.95         P < 0.5
#>      Full        -   0.02-0.03 0.01, 0.04-0.30
#>  Age only        -           -       0.01-0.30
summary(e$p_best)
#> P(best): Full, Age only; binary, n = 500, prior improper Beta(0, 0), 1000 posterior draws
#> Most likely best: Full 0.01-0.03, Age only 0.04-0.30

#> # 20 more thresholds; summary(x, thresholds = ) to choose
set.seed(1)
summary(evsi(res1, res2, future_n = c(500, 1000, 2000)))
#> EVSI: Full, Age only; binary, n = 500, 1000 posterior draws
#> Before the future study (as for EVPI): prior improper Beta(0, 0), updated with the validation data (n = 500)
#> Future study: 500, 1,000 or 2,000 more patients, drawn from that distribution; then the prior is updated with the validation data and the future study together
